Samples from the work.

Each one shows the problem, what I did about it and the tool it lives in. Click a screenshot to read it full size.

Notion

Daily Execution

The problem

Tasks scattered across people, with no single view of what is due, who owns it and what is waiting.

What I did

One Notion table. Each task has a category (sales, operations, marketing, support, admin), an owner, a due date and a link to that day's end of day report. Views for open tasks and by status.

Tools

Notion

Notion

Follow-Up Tracker

The problem

Follow-ups that slip because the due date and the owner live in someone's head.

What I did

A tracker where every follow-up has a due date, an owner, a priority and the deal it belongs to, with an Overdue view and a By Status view.

Tools

Notion

Notion

EOD Reports

The problem

Blockers that only surface once something is already late.

What I did

A short end of day report per person: what is blocked, what needs attention, and the tasks it relates to, linked back to Daily Execution.

Tools

Notion

Trello

Sales and Follow-Up Board

The problem

Leads going quiet somewhere between first contact and a booked meeting.

What I did

A Trello board with a column for each stage: New Lead, Contacted, Follow-Up Due, Follow-Up Sent and Meeting Booked, with due dates on the cards.

Tools

Trello

Lead generation

Cold Call List

The problem

Outreach needs a clean list of the right people, not a pile of names.

What I did

A Google Sheets list built per target group, with title, region, country, email and LinkedIn profile for every contact. Names and contact details are hidden here.

Tools

Google Sheets, LinkedIn

SOPs

Workflow SOP

The problem

Steps that only work when the right person remembers them.

What I did

A written workflow SOP for pre onboarding: numbered steps, who does each one, and what to do in each case, such as recurring payments.

Tools

Google Docs
